speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where you are feeling the neck and arm pain, and which specific fingers have the tingling sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain or tingling radiate specifically down one arm, or is it symmetrical in both? I also need to know if you have noticed any difficulty with fine motor tasks, like buttoning a shirt or writing.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the presence of fasciculations and absent reflexes, I need to rule out motor neuron disease. Do you experience any sensory loss, such as numbness or reduced sensation to light touch, in your hands or arms? REQUEST TEST: EMG

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG is normal, motor neuron disease is unlikely, and the presence of paresthesias points toward a sensory component rather than pure motor neuron loss. I suspect cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy; do you experience any balance issues, clumsiness in your legs, or changes in bowel or bladder control? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a syrinx, which explains the dissociated sensory loss and motor findings consistent with syringomyelia. Given your history of a motor vehicle accident three years ago, this is likely a post-traumatic syrinx. DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-traumatic Syringomyelia
